summary: 100-ft WPA-era steel fire tower on Greene-Sullivan State Forest, erected 1940-41; listed as gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed gone by firelookout.org; indianafiretowers.com says not standing, but its author has not visited the site.
facts.agency: Indiana Department of Conservation, Division of Forestry (builder); tower on Greene-Sullivan State Forest

access.note: The state forest has public trails; no source describes the former tower site.

events.note: State annual report says a 100-foot steel fire tower was erected on the forest; WPA foundation work had started in December 1940.
Outdoor Indiana list of state towers in District 3 includes Pleasantville.
Table of towers at parks and forests lists Greene-Sullivan forest; the article says few if any towers were still used for fire detection.

evidence.supports: June 1940: Division of Forestry planned a tower west of Pleasantville; announced by state department
evidence.quote: A fire-tower is to be built west of Pleasantville by the Division of Forestry of the Indiana State Department of Conservation, according to a preliminary announcement received here.

evidence.supports: WPA funds helped build the tower
evidence.quote: The work of building the tower is to be done through the assistance of Federal WPA funds

evidence.supports: July 1940: tower to stand north of Pleasantville
evidence.quote: The tower, being erected by the Division of Forestry, will be located north pf Pleasantville.

Protection from forest fire will be extended to approximately 125,000 acres of land surrounding the Green-Sullivan County State Forest as the result of erection of a 100-foot steel tower at the forest.

evidence.supports: December 1940: WPA started the tower foundation
evidence.quote: Installation of the tower foundation has been started by WPA under the supervision of the division of forestry.

evidence.supports: Planned visibility radius of about ten miles
evidence.quote: This tower will have a visibility radius of approximately 10 miles

evidence.supports: 1941 annual report: tower erected on Greene-Sullivan forest
evidence.quote: a one hundred foot steel fire tower was erected

evidence.supports: January 1960 Outdoor Indiana list of state towers in District 3
evidence.quote: This OI article from January 1960 says there are 13 state towers in District 3

evidence.supports: Pleasantville is named on the 1960 list
1978 table lists the Greene-Sullivan forest among towers
By 1978 few if any towers still used for fire detection
evidence.quote: By this time, few if any of the towers are still being used for fire detection.

evidence.supports: Forest Service page places the tower on Greene-Sullivan State Forest
evidence.quote: Sullivan Pleasantville Tower Greene-Sullivan State Forest

evidence.supports: Database lists the tower as gone
Not standing; author has not visited the site
evidence.quote: Condition: Not standing (I have not visited this site yet)

evidence.supports: State forest has trails used by hikers and horseback riders
evidence.quote: Hikers and horseback riders are advised to wear hunter orange or other bright clothing while on trails during hunting season.

corrections.proposed: Indiana Department of Conservation, Division of Forestry (builder); tower on Greene-Sullivan State Forest
corrections.why: The 1940 papers credit the Division of Forestry of the state Department of Conservation with building the tower. The Forest Service list names the property Greene-Sullivan State Forest, which is a state forest, not a county one.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A June 1940 paper put the tower west of Pleasantville and a July 1940 paper put it north. No later source settles the spot, so the record gives only the town.
December 1940 reports describe foundation work and a planned tower; the 1941 annual report says it was erected. The record uses 1941.

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today; the indianafiretowers author has not visited. Staffing and fire history are not in these sources. The 1940 items are quoted secondhand through Forest Lookouts. The 1978 table is read as listing a tower for the forest, not confirmed as this tower.
